R-1.title: Stale generation-time baseline for connectors that cannot seed
R-1.fix: The runner observes the world at case start when the connector cannot seed, records baseline OBSERVED_AT_START and the initial state hash, and projects against that. Compile observes the demonstrated delta: argument-to-field bindings, the created or changed count, and a changed record's identifier. The generator emits a value-filtered success__performed check and a success__exactly_as_demonstrated count check. After AFTER-1 showed that an agent doing the job and also deleting another record passed, deletions of the focus entity are held to the demonstration as well (P8).
R-1.rerunEvidence: AFTER-1 (f4145bb): 0 of the 11 R-1 cases reproduce under either rule. AFTER-2 (26d1e6a product sources): 0 reproductions among the R-1 cases that ran; see R1_CASES_RUN and R1_REPRODUCTIONS in after-results.json. Correct agents now pass against a world observed at case start, and duplicates, wrong values, wrong entities and extra deletions fail.
R-1.regressionFoundAndFixed: AFTER-1: SQ-W1-06 and SQ-W1B-06 (extra delete) TRUE_POSITIVE at the baseline only through R-1, FALSE_NEGATIVE at f4145bb; fixed by 65bbaed and re-measured in AFTER-2
R-1.limits: Changes to other records and the identity of a demonstrated deletion are not checked; only the focus entity is held to the demonstrated delta.

R-2.title: No independent oracle
R-2.fix: MCP and OpenAPI connectors accept a verifier connection. Its tools are exposed only to verification as verifier:<tool>, never offered to the agent, and every case reports evidenceIndependence INDEPENDENT, SELF_REPORTED or NONE.
R-2.reproduction: remediation/repro/cli.repro.test.ts (a verifier on an MCP connector was silently dropped at 07dda8c)
R-2.limits: A capability, not a change to the frozen benchmark: the re-run keeps the audit's single-connector specs, so every re-run verdict is labelled SELF_REPORTED.

R-3.title: Column-cell result shapes induce a value-keyed entity
R-3.fix: canonicalisePayload unwraps exact {kind|type, value} tagged scalars and keeps a wrapped list entry under its list's name; induced entity names are deduplicated; ties in identifier choice prefer whole numbers and whitespace-free strings.
R-3.rerunEvidence: sqlite W1/W1b induce Row keyed by id (baseline: Id keyed by value) with value-bound checks. In AFTER-2 every SQ-W1-* and SQ-W1B-* case matches the oracle on every attempt: correct agents TRUE_NEGATIVE, missing action, duplicate, wrong value, wrong entity and extra delete TRUE_POSITIVE. The audit specs disable the quality check for sqlite, so no kill-rate figure exists for these suites.

R-4.title: 15 s case budget below the 20 s tool timeout; timeouts indistinguishable from failures
R-4.fix: Outcome classes PASS, FAIL, ABSTAIN, TIMED_OUT, AGENT_FAILURE, HARNESS_FAILURE; typed agent timeout; project budgets toolCallMs 20000 and caseMs 60000 validated so caseMs >= toolCallMs + 5000; --case-timeout; the agent process timeout is derived from the case budget.
R-4.rerunEvidence: EM-GM-06 (injected lost response) now reaches the retry inside the 60 s budget and is TRUE_POSITIVE on every attempt in AFTER-1 and AFTER-2 (baseline: the 15 s budget killed it before the retry; FALSE_POSITIVE). Timeouts are reported as TIMED_OUT, never as a verification FAIL: EM-LLM-01 and SQ-LLM-01 in AFTER-1.
R-4.limits: A slow agent that does the job but exceeds the budget is TIMED_OUT, not PASS (SQ-LLM-01 in AFTER-1); the original scoring rule counts that as a false positive.

R-5.title: Instruction from the tool description; a dual-purpose tool's last call becomes the primary action
R-5.fix: The demonstration records whether each non-read-only call changed the nominated reads; the primary action and its arguments come from the last call that changed state; the project goal is the contract goal.
R-5.rerunEvidence: sqlite W1 contract: goal is the project goal (baseline: the execute tool's doc comment); case inputs are the INSERT (baseline: SELECT * FROM tasks ORDER BY id). Home: tmp/rigorrun-audit/after-homes/home-sqlite-w1, trace remediation/after/traces/sqlite-mcp/w1-setup Same in AFTER-2.

R-6.title: No headless project setup
R-6.fix: rigorrun setup <spec.json> drives connect, reads, demonstration, schema answers, compile, rules, suite, optional quality check and agents in-process; credentials come from environment variables the spec names.
R-6.rerunEvidence: the external held-out sqlite and GreenMail projects are created with rigorrun setup; docs/V1_GAP_AUDIT.md lists it as WORKING

R-7.title: verify --needs-credential documented but not wired
R-7.fix: The repeatable flag is parsed and reaches the planner as NEEDS_CREDENTIAL.
R-7.unresolved: The verify sandbox image is still Node-only, so Python, Rust and unpublished servers such as the three audited targets still cannot go through verify.

R-8.title: JSON-in-text passes the read probe but yields no records at demonstration
R-8.fix: One normalizeCallResult (structured, json_text, text, empty, error) used by the probe, demonstration capture, compile inputs and runtime reads; JSON text is data only with an object or array top level; prose at run time is missing evidence, never an empty world.
R-8.rerunEvidence: Worktide W2 and W3 compile and build suites in AFTER-1 and AFTER-2 (baseline: both refused at compile with "returned text rather than structured records").
R-8.openAfterFix: N-1 (open-regressions.json): the newly built Worktide suites key a time-report group by its minutes value and fail their own quality check. Measured on the external held-out set: EH-WT-03, an agent that creates two time entries instead of one, passes. The normalisation defect (R-8) is fixed; Worktide verdicts through these suites are not trustworthy.
